newsitem.title: CHILE: Two flee from secretive German colony in Chile.
newsitem.headline: Two flee from secretive German colony in Chile.

text.p: Two young men have fled from a German enclave in southern Chile whose leader is accused of child abuse and are seeking refuge at the German embassy, Deputy Interior Minister Belisario Velasco said on Tuesday.
Velasco said the men, a 24-year old German identified as Tobias Muller and Chilean Zalo Luna, were staying at the house of a first secretary at the mission.

Muller, the only colonist known to have fled in the last 10 years from the secretive settlement known as Villa Baviera, is being looked after by embassy officials, said German ambassador Werner Reichenbaum.
"Mr. Tobias Muller has fled from Villa Baviera and is under the protection of the authorities," Reichenbaum told reporters.
"In the past the colony has made attempts to recapture people who escape, and they must be protected."
Muller and Luna made their way to the embassy from the enclave, which lies 200 miles (340 km) south of Santiago, without the help of diplomatic officials, he said.
Local media reported that the men escaped from the heavily-guarded colony during celebrations to mark the 36th anniversary of the founding of Colonia Dignidad (Dignity Colony).
The settlers have sought a court order for the release of the men who they claim were detained by Chilean police.

La Tercera newspaper said that Muller, whose mother tried unsuccessfully to have her son returned to Germany from the colony in 1988, worked as a teacher at the settlement's boarding school. Luna helped at weekend youth camps run by the colonists.

The settlement's founder, Paul Schaefer, is the subject of an international arrest warrant after being charged with sexually abusing at least five boys living at the boarding school. He and other leaders also face charges of illegal detention of children, obstruction of justice and tax fraud.
A series of raids by police in recent months at the settlement failed to find the 76-year-old Schaefer, who has not been seen in public for several years.
Defectors from the colony say residents are not allowed to read newspapers or watch television, their mail is censored and youngsters are subjected to unusual punishments by Schaefer.

"It is undoubtable that there has been an irregular situation in the colony for many years ... (including) offences against children as evidenced by the accusations from their families," said Velasco.
Claims of abuses first emerged in the 1960s when a young settler Wolfgang Muller escaped from the colony which lies in the foothills of the Andes near the town of Parral.

The colony was set up by Schaefer, a corporal in the German army in the Second World War, in 1961. Schaefer fled to Chile after being charged with sexually assaulting boys at an orphanage he set up in Germany.
Human rights groups have charged the settlement was used as a detention centre in the 1970s for political prisoners during General Augusto Pinochet's military rule.
